motion.name: state

motion.name: lit-in

motion.name: site-entrance

motion.name: site-reveal

motion.name: site-cta

motion.name: site-ghost-sweep

motion.name: site-disclosure

motion.name: site-film
motion.value: muted, in view only; fill follows currentTime / duration

motion.name: site-header
motion.purpose: Marketing world: header padding, ground and rule once scrolled; opaque, no blur.

narrative.overview:
The page is a sentence the buyer completes, « Je cherche une villa… », and the residence answers: the lots that fit stay lit on the 3D view and the list keeps only them. Everything else steps back. The ground is near-black, surfaces are raised by a few percent of white, and structure is drawn with white hairlines. The only colour that speaks is the promoter's (champagne when none is set), and it comes from data, not from the stylesheet.

It is an app, not a brochure: a fixed frame (top bar, stage, bottom action bar) with one scrolling column inside, built for a phone opened from a WhatsApp link. Density is compact; a lot is a register line, not a card. The image is never dressed up: no rounded frame, no margin, no overlay beyond the controls it needs.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground, white hairlines, one data-driven brand colour.
The promoter's font carries names, the sentence and lot numbers; Inter carries the interface.
One corner (10px) for buttons and blocks; pills only say a status.
Phone first: a 52px top bar, the 3D view full width, a fixed action bar at the bottom.
Lots as register lines: number, facts, status, price at the right.
French and English everywhere. No scroll-driven effects; movement lasts 150 to 300 ms.

rules.name: The Borrowed Colour Rule
rules.body: The colour belongs to the promoter. Always write `var(--brand)` and `var(--brand-contrast)`; never a champagne hex, never a Tailwind `primary`.

rules.name: The Three Statuses Rule
rules.body: Brand is available, amber is reserved, graphite is sold, identically on the view, in the list, on the sheet and in the legend. No fourth meaning borrows one of these colours.

rules.name: The White Means Chosen Rule
rules.body: In a rail or a group of choices, the chosen item is white with black text. The brand colour is not a selection colour.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The brand font says names, the sentence, lot numbers and key figures. Every control, value, price and label is Inter. A price is never in the brand font.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or stack (lot numbers, prices, counts, percentages) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Blur Belongs To Images Rule
rules.body: Background blur and shadow appear only on a control that sits on a photo, a render or a viewer. On the page's own black, a surface is flat with a hairline.

rules.name: The Pill Is A Status Rule
rules.body: If it is fully rounded, it states available, reserved or sold. Buttons, filters and tabs are never pills.

rules.name: The Stage Rule (marketing site)
rules.body: Champagne is spent as a whole surface or as a precise mark, never as a thin decoration: a stage that carries the product, the closing band, the primary action, one phrase per heading, and what REV does. What the model and the brochure do stays muted grey; a neutral fact never borrows champagne.

rules.name: The Ink On Champagne Rule (marketing site)
rules.body: On a champagne ground everything is black: text, the filled action (`ink`: black with a champagne label), the outlined action (`inkGhost`), underlines and focus rings. White and champagne-on-champagne never appear there.

rules.name: The Spec Sheet Voice Rule (marketing site)
rules.body: Space Grotesk names things (headings, functions, scenes, questions, numerals); Inter explains them. Labels are sentence case at 12px or more; no tracked capitals anywhere.

rules.name: The Plain Title Rule (marketing site)
rules.body: Nothing sits above a title: no eyebrow, no kicker, no label (the `eyebrow` prop is still accepted at call sites and never rendered). One phrase is champagne. A one-sentence title loses its final period through `headline()`.

rules.name: The Lit Product Rule (marketing site)
rules.body: Shadows are cast by the product (a phone, a screen, a popover of that screen), not by the page's own blocks. A block of content on the ground is never raised.

rules.name: The No Pill Rule (marketing site)
rules.body: A labelled control (button, filter, tab) is never fully rounded on the marketing site; statuses in the illustration are a dot and a word.

dos: Do take the colour and the display font from `var(--brand)`, `var(--brand-contrast)` and `font-brand`; check a new surface with a second brand colour and a serif brand font.
Do design at 390 wide first: 52px top bar, full-width view, fixed bottom bar with the main action.
Do use the 10px corner for buttons and blocks, 12px for a rail around 9 to 10px controls, full rounding for statuses only.
Do say a status the same way everywhere: brand, amber, graphite, each with its word.
Do write every text in French and English, and give every number tabular figures.
Do keep images edge to edge and untouched; put only translucent controls on them.
Do keep « Propulsé par » and the REV logo on every public page.
Do respect reduced motion; keep movement between 150 and 300ms on colour, opacity or a few pixels.
Marketing site: do show the product at work on a champagne stage: one dark object, a soft shadow under it, 14px corners, edge to edge on phones.
Marketing site: do close a page with the champagne band and use the `ink` and `inkGhost` actions on it.
Marketing site: do open every part with a 70% rule and let the heading speak for itself, with one champagne phrase; pass titles through `headline()`.
Marketing site: do put functions, services and reasons on register lines, name in Space Grotesk, explanation in Inter.
Marketing site: do use the 10px corner for every action; 48px for CTAs, 32px for text links.
Marketing site: do keep films muted, in view only, and silent under reduced motion or data saving, with a play button instead.
Marketing site: do write every text in French and English and keep « Propulsé par » with the REV logo on the page.
donts: Don't hard-code champagne or use the stylesheet's `primary`: the colour is the promoter's.
Don't use the brand colour for a selected tab or choice; white says chosen.
Don't make buttons, filters or tabs into pills.
Don't put a lot in a card; a lot is a line.
Don't set prices, labels or controls in the brand font.
Don't tie any effect to scrolling, and don't bring the marketing site's reveals or champagne stages here.
Don't set a label in tracked capitals, and don't zoom an image or a lot tag under the pointer.
Don't add shadow or blur to a surface that sits on the page's black.
Marketing site: don't put a label, eyebrow or kicker above a heading, and don't set labels in tracked capitals.
Marketing site: don't use gradient text, glass surfaces, glows, or blur on anything that is not sitting on a film or a photo.
Marketing site: don't lay functions out as a grid of icon cards; a card tone is for a product illustration on a stage.
Marketing site: don't put white or champagne text on a champagne ground; it takes black.
Marketing site: don't spend champagne on neutral facts or on what the model and brochure do.
Marketing site: don't make a labelled button, filter or tab a pill.
Marketing site: don't zoom, lift or float anything under the pointer, and don't lengthen reveals beyond 0.6s, 16px and 4px of blur.
Marketing site: don't bring these `site-*` tokens or the theme `primary` into `src/components/public/**`.
